title: Shivchat
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Bava Kamma 91b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.91b.19): “Rabbi Chanina said: My son Shivchat died only because he cut down a fig tree before its time.” Dikdukei Soferim reads “Shikhchat my son.”

In [Bava Batra 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.26a.11) Rashi explains: “Shivchat Beri” was his name. There, at [126b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.126b.11): a certain man came before Rabbi Chanina and said to him, “I have a presumption about this one (whom he came to testify about) that he is a firstborn.” He said to him, “How do you know?” He said: “When people came to his father, he would say to them, ‘Go to Shivchat my son, who is a firstborn, and whose spittle heals.’” The Rashbam explains “Shivchat Beri” as the firstborn’s name, and this is not the son of Rabbi Chanina mentioned in Bava Batra 26.[^1]
[Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3271&lang=en) already discussed at length whether his name was “Shivchat Beri” or whether his name was Shivchat; see there.

notes.text: Bava Kamma has Shivchat. The consulted Bava Batra text and both glosses use Shikhchat. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Batra.26a.11.1) says that the phrase is his name; [Rashbam](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashbam_on_Bava_Batra.126b.11.3) calls it the firstborn’s name and distinguishes him from Rabbi Chanina’s son. Heilprin argues that Beri was part of the name and that the two notices concern the same person.
